New Motivation:
Higher total daily energy intake (TDEI) can contribute to an increase in group-level BMI because, on average, consuming more calories than are expended increases the likelihood of fat accumulation at the population level. However, the relationship is influenced by factors such as metabolic rate, physical activity, and genetic differences, so higher TDEI does not universally or inevitably result in higher BMI for all individuals within a group.

Corrected Motivation:
"Physical activity level directly increases Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) since physical activities require energy beyond what the body expends at rest.
